question: Does the register-file hash actually CATCH a planted register divergence at a guest-logical-control point, refuse to fire inside a tool handler, and avoid passing by emitting nothing?
comparison_path: hermit run --strict --detlog-regs --verify --verify-strict (the product's own double-run INFO comparator)
plant_mechanism: RDRAND, which Detcore masks in CPUID but never determinizes, parked in a callee-saved register (r13) held across a syscall and never printed
defect_found_and_fixed: At cadence>=5 a one-control-point guest emitted ZERO register samples and the planted divergence PASSED. Fixed by counting samples per thread (ThreadStats::regs_sample_index) so index 0 is always sampled.
not_established: Cross-backend register parity was NOT measured: only ptrace was exercised. The boundary claim is verified against handler traffic within ptrace, not against an in-guest-handler backend (sabre/liteinst/e9patch).
Coverage is syscall-exit control points only. Signal delivery to the guest and thread start are plausible guest-logical-control points and are NOT sampled.
rcx/r11 and the segment selectors are excluded from the hash by design, so a divergence confined to them is invisible.
